variables.meaning: the solubility product constant, the equilibrium constant for the dissolution of a slightly soluble ionic compound
the reaction quotient for the dissolution of a slightly soluble ionic compound
the molar concentration of the cation M<sup>m+</sup> in a saturated solution
the molar concentration of the anion X<sup>n–</sup> in a saturated solution
the number of cations in the formula M<sub>p</sub>X<sub>q</sub>
the number of anions in the formula M<sub>p</sub>X<sub>q</sub>
the change in concentration defined by the ICE table; for a simple dissolution, the molar solubility
the formation constant (stability constant) for a complex ion
the dissociation constant for a complex ion, the reciprocal of its formation constant
the equilibrium constant for the net reaction of two coupled equilibria
the second ionization constant of carbonic acid, for bicarbonate ion

the formation of Cu(CN)<sub>2</sub><sup>–</sup> from Cu<sup>+</sup> and CN<sup>–</sup>
a complex ion and the reverse of its formation reaction

glossary.definition: effect on equilibrium when a substance with an ion in common with the dissolved species is added to the solution; causes a decrease in the solubility of an ionic species, or a decrease in the ionization of a weak acid or base
solubility of a compound expressed in units of moles per liter (mol/L)
process in which ions are separated using differences in their solubility with a given precipitating reagent
equilibrium constant for the dissolution of an ionic compound
ion consisting of a central atom surrounding molecules or ions called ligands via coordinate covalent bonds

equilibrium constant for the decomposition of a complex ion into its components
(also, stability constant) equilibrium constant for the formation of a complex ion from its components
any species that can accept a pair of electrons and form a coordinate covalent bond
compound or ion that contains a coordinate covalent bond between a Lewis acid and a Lewis base
reactions involving the formation of coordinate covalent bonds
any species that can donate a pair of electrons and form a coordinate covalent bond
molecule or ion acting as a Lewis base in complex ion formation; bonds to the central atom of the complex
system characterized the simultaneous establishment of two or more equilibrium reactions sharing one or more reactant or product
